title: How a Tsunami Races Across the Ocean
description: What sets off a tsunami, how fast it travels in deep water and why it grows near shore.
narration: What turns an underwater shake into a giant wave? Tsunamis are waves set off by undersea earthquakes or volcanic eruptions. Landslides under the water or along the coast can also trigger them. Over deep ocean, the waves can race along at up to 800 kilometres per hour. NOAA says they may match the speed of jet planes. The speed of a tsunami depends on ocean depth, not on distance from the source. Near the shore, friction with the rising seafloor slows the waves down. As they slow, the waves bunch closer together and grow taller.
